author: GamingBolt
description:
The follow up to 2021’s Grime is here, and it's been a pleasure to play. Grime 2 takes the best of the previous game and weaves it into a fresh new experience that manages to be compelling enough to make you attempt multiple runs through levels and battles that are going to be humbling until you learn to wield your skillset effectively. 

It's all framed within the context of an abstract world with an obscure, slow-burning story that makes this one a very engaging addition to the platforming genre, and a finely balanced and polished title to boot. Join us as we take you through what it's like to play, and let you decide if it's one you want to try out for yourself.
title: GRIME 2 Review - 2026's Most Unexpected Masterstroke

author: GamingBolt
description:
Samson is inching ever closer to its April 2026 release date, and it has managed to gain 250,000 wishlists over the time since it was first revealed to the world. That’s quite a number for what could be easy to write off as a mildly interesting indie, and the game probably has its solid promotional materials to thank for that milestone. 

But do those materials manage to convey what’s truly exciting about this game? We think that there’s a lot of nuance behind the impression that Samson is going for, and that it’s going to surprise its players with an experience that pushes against their expectations of an exciting crime sandbox, instead giving them a world that seems designed to force errors out of them, thereby making their very survival a struggle. 

And that is the part of the game that we’re really excited to dive into. Join us as we look under the hood of this one, and give you even more reasons to dive into it as soon as it’s out.
title: You Are ABSOLUTELY NOT READY For Samson: A Tyndalston Story

author: GamingBolt
description:
Solving puzzles in Crimson Desert can be time-consuming, tedious, and very often frustrating. So why the hell is it so darn satisfying when we piece together a solution in a situation where it felt like the game was actively working against us? 

Because that’s what the greatest Greymanes do. They persevere in the face of impossible odds, even if those odds involve figuring out how to get a drawing on the wall to align so we could unlock a way to kick our opponents as we descended from the skies above them. 

Love them or hate them, Crimson Desert’s approach to its puzzles is an interesting way to smirk at existing traditions and give its players a level of trust that other games have hesitated to adopt. Join us as we look at why that’s great news for you, and for open worlds in general as they now have a new benchmark to aspire to.

title: Crimson Desert’s Puzzles Need A Different Brain For Each One
